title: Sancristóbal 2022 · Passive auditory EEG
citation: Sancristóbal et al. (2022). Slow Resting State Fluctuations Enhance Neuronal and Behavioral Responses to Looming Sounds. Brain Topography, 35(1), 121–141.
notes: Published study settings are available for inspection. See the source-backed method and remaining execution requirements.

published_method.audio: A 44.1 kHz pink noise sample lasts 3100 ms. The approach variant increases exponentially from 55 to 70 dB SPL. The flat variant is 62.5 dB SPL.
published_method.preceded_by_rest: Two five-minute eyes-closed resting EEG runs precede this assessment.
published_method.response: Attend to sounds blindfolded with eyes closed and without a manual response.
published_method.eeg: MR-compatible 64-channel BrainAmp with FCz reference, Iz ground and 5000 Hz sampling in Philips 3 T Achieva. Synchronizer links scanner and recording clocks. Analysis downsamples to 500 Hz and addresses imaging and physiological artifacts.
published_method.analysis: Compare evoked spectral power for looming and flat, alongside resting autocorrelation and behavioral facilitation.
